sentences.text: 12 19-04-2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Learned counsel for the parties have referred to the detailed order dated 12.4.2019 passed in the instant case as also to the counter affidavit filed on behalf of respondent nos.1 and Learned counsel for the petitioner refers to Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2015 whereby in exercise of powers conferred under section 113 of the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013, this order was brought into force with effect from 1.9.2015.

The relevant part of the order is quoted herein below for ready reference:-
"1.(1) This Order may be called the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Removal of Difficulties) Order,
2015.

sentences.text: (2) It shall come into force with effect from the 1st day of September, 2015.

2. The provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, relating to the determination of compensation in accordance with the First Schedule, rehabilitation and resettlement in accordance with the Second Schedule and Patna High Court CWJC No.6988 of 2018(12) dt.19-04-2023 infrastructure amenities in accordance with the Third Schedule shall apply to all cases of land acquisition under the enactments specified in the Fourth Schedule to the said Act."

Learned counsel for the respondents submits that so far as the acquisition in the instant case is concerned, the same is not a complete acquisition of right, title and possession of the petitioner but only right of user is acquired by the authorities while acquiring land under the Petroleum and Ajay Kumar Singh @ Ajay Singh @ Mantu ... vs The Union Of India on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138805330/
2 Minerals Pipelines Act, 1962.
Before proceeding further it would be relevant to quote section 113 of the Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013:-
"113. Power to remove difficulties.-(1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Part, the Central Government may, by order, make such provisions or give such directions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act as may be appears to it to be necessary or expedient for the removal of the difficulty:
Provided that no such power shall be exercised after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.
(2) Every order made under this Section shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament."
Patna High Court CWJC No.6988 of 2018(12) dt.19-04-2023 Let a further counter affidavit be filed by the respondent-Union of India as to whether the requirement as mentioned in section 113(2) of the Act of 2013 was complied with or not.
Put up this case after four weeks.
(Partha Sarthy, J) Shiv/-
